label: ndcgtree16

budget_change.why: 15 was inherited from the genre experiment's turn accounting, where the genre question consumed one of 16 turns. Nothing in this tree consumes an extra turn, so the budget is max(BUDGETS) = 16, the length the static orders were built to.
budget_change.note: The tree STRUCTURE is untouched -- same nodes, same splitters, same leaves, same depth. Only each leaf's greedy tail gained one question, by resuming its banked CELF heap.

comparator.headline: greedy_static_policyB_combined
comparator.supersedes: This order SUPERSEDES the `combined` arm of greedy_static_i26c.json as the static comparator. That arm was SELECTED under the retired policy-A candidate mask (its intercept_eval 0.13139/0.02343 is the policy-A intercept; policy B is 0.1586/0.0282), so comparing a policy-B arm against it carried a selection-protocol offset -- measured at +0.00093 full at K=1 -- inside every K>=2 number. This rebuild uses the SAME pool (500 pop items + 500 answerable concepts, items first), the SAME objective (cohort-mean held-out full NDCG@10), the SAME 10,000 canonical validation users and the SAME certified stack, under POLICY B. It reuses the completed CELF heap the tree's root node built, which is exactly this search's seed pass.

size_vs_gain.interpretation: A NEGATIVE rho is the overfitting signature the genre experiment was built to detect: small leaves gaining most means the per-leaf orders are fitting noise on the SELECTION cohort. These are in-sample numbers -- the leaves' orders were chosen on the very users being scored. Only the TEST cohort settles it.

in_sample_warning: SELECTION-COHORT NUMBERS. The leaves' orders were chosen on the same 10,000 validation users they are scored on. The TEST cohort has not been built, loaded or touched by this job.
